playbook.intent: Feature flags have accumulated in the platform faster than anyone retires them, and several have sat at a partial rollout for months with nobody watching. The weekly review ends when every open flag has been ramped, held, rolled back or decommissioned in the platform itself rather than only in the review notes, and the flags past the kill threshold are queued for deletion.
playbook.scope: Tech lead + PM review every open feature flag weekly. For each: keep dark / ramp / GA / kill. Decision criteria are explicit (SLO impact, error rate, adoption metric). Flags that drift out of lifecycle get auto-flagged for deletion.

success-criteria.criterion: Every live flag appears in the inventory with an owner, an age and its current rollout percentage
Each flag carries a written call this week — keep dark, ramp, GA or kill — justified against SLO impact, error rate or the adoption metric
The flag configuration in the platform matches the calls that were made, so no decision exists only on paper
Any ramp of ten percent or more has an hour of dashboard watching logged behind it, with the pause or revert recorded if a threshold broke

stage.name: Score Active Flags

tasks.task: List every flag, owner, age, and current rollout %
Tag each flag: ramping, in-test, stuck, decommission-ready
Flag any flag older than the kill-threshold

stage.decision-gate: Advance only when every active flag has a tag and an owner.

stage.name: Decide per Flag

tasks.task: For each flag: ramp +X% / hold / roll back / decommission
Verify the decision against business and ops dashboards
Communicate the per-flag decision to owners

stage.decision-gate: Advance only when every flag has a written decision this week.

stage.name: Execute
stage.intent: Touch the flags, not just the doc.

tasks.task: Apply each flag decision in the platform
Watch dashboards for 1 hour after any ramp ≥10%
Pause or revert on threshold breach

stage.decision-gate: Required output: a logged execution per decision.
